newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates dip in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates dip in liquid market.

text.p: Philippine interbank call loan rates dipped to an average of 12.53125 percent on Friday from the previous day's 12.59375 as most banks were liquid with the end of the reserve week, traders said.
Rates, however, were higher than last Friday's 10.53125 after the Central Bank raised its overnight borrwoing rate by 2.25 percentage points to 12.50 percent to quell currency speculation.
"The market has remained liquid," a trader said, adding that interest rates were higher only because the Central Bank placed the floor on rates at 12.50 percent.
Volume thinned to 11.597 billion pesos from 13.977 billion. Out of the 48 participating financial institutions, 24 were lenders.

Due to the higher benchmark rate of the Central Bank, traders said there was little demand for one-year bills at the secondary market since banks had opted to lend their money on an overnight basis where rates were higher.

Next week, the trader said interest rates could move lower as more liquidity comes into the system. The market expects maturities of Treasury notes in the amount of 7 billion to 10 billion pesos on Sept 11, she said.
